# Cooling upgrades

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Remove an existing secondary transmission cooler, install a larger B&M unit, then mount a fan between them. [t25]

[Partial] Swap the stock auxiliary transmission cooler for a Z1 19-row stacked plate cooler and connect the return line using a 5/16-inch barbed connector. [t98]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Swap the stock auxiliary transmission cooler for a Z1 19-row stacked plate cooler.
2. Connect the return line using a 5/16-inch barbed connector to link the stock line to the new cooler's supplied line.

_Procedure reported by [t98]._

## Parts

- [Partial] 5/16-inch Barbed Connector: For the return line connection [t98]
- B&M Cooler: Larger size from Summit Racing [t25]
- [Partial] Z1 Transmission Cooler: 19-row stacked plate design [t98]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Mount a fan between the new cooler and the radiator. [t25]
- [Partial] Attach the fan to the back side of the cooler so it sucks air through the core before pushing it into the radiator. [t25]
- [Partial] Use a 5/16-inch barbed connector for the return line if it is easier than the stock method. [t98]
